audience: An eco-minded or budget-conscious parent or grandparent buying (or building) a child's very first bike as a handmade, natural gift — and schools/education partners who want the most sustainable, lowest-cost build.

positioning.title: A first bike made of plants, not plastic.
positioning.lede: Our most sustainable and most affordable balance bike: bamboo tubes joined with natural flax fibre and resin — no metal lugs, no carbon, no plastic shop bike. It's the same first bike a parent builds for their own child on our prison programme, so the one you make at home helps fund a place for a family to be reunited.

who_for.title: Parents who want the greenest first bike
who_for.body: 100% natural materials — bamboo and flax, no carbon fibre and no plastic. The most sustainable, most hand-made bike we sell, and a keepsake to pass down rather than throw away.

who_for.title: Anyone watching the budget
who_for.body: The flax build skips the CNC and 3D-printed lugs, so it's our most affordable kit. A meaningful handmade first bike without an adult-frame price tag.

who_for.title: Schools, colleges & partnership programmes
who_for.body: Built around natural-fibre jointing and basic hand tools, the flax kit suits group and education builds where sustainability and cost matter most. Talk to us about partnership pricing.

faq.q: What age and size is this for?
faq.a: Designed for children roughly aged 2–5, as a balance (pedal-free) first bike. Fit depends on your child's inside-leg measurement more than age — send us their height and inside leg and we'll confirm it suits them. (FLAG: confirm exact age/height/inside-leg range and minimum age with James.)

faq.q: Is it light enough for a toddler to handle?
faq.a: Bamboo is naturally light and the balance frame is small, so it's made to be manageable for little legs. We don't want to publish a weight we haven't measured — please confirm the finished weight in kg before this goes live. (FLAG: real weight needed; likely stated nowhere in BBC source.)

faq.q: Why choose flax over the lugged balance bike?
faq.a: Two reasons: it's greener and cheaper. The flax kit joins the bamboo with natural plant fibre and resin instead of metal or 3D-printed lugs — so it's 100% natural materials (bamboo and flax, no carbon), the most sustainable build we make, and our most affordable. The lugged version uses metal/printed lug joints, which some builders prefer for the look and a slightly more guided build. Both make the same pedal-free first bike.

faq.q: How hard is the build, and how long does it take?
faq.a: It's our simplest kit — around 10–15 hours, comfortably spread over a weekend or two. No power tools: just basic hand tools (hacksaw, files, sandpaper, tape) and a work surface. You bond the bamboo tubes with epoxy and wrap each joint in flax fibre. Most builders start with zero experience, and our community of 4,000+ can help if you get stuck.

faq.q: Is it safe and strong enough for a child?
faq.a: The flax-and-bamboo frame is sealed and tough — bamboo runs around 28,000 PSI tensile strength (comparable to mild steel), under 1% failure across 4,000+ builds, and tested with Swansea University. As with any child's bike, fit a helmet and supervise early rides.
